The *Bhāvanāvāra* (Ya 9.3) is a section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Like other analytical divisions of the *Yamaka*, the section applies paired sets of questions and catechetical formulas to elucidate doctrinal categories, in this case focusing on the aspect of mental cultivation or development (*bhāvanā*).

According to the automated text-reuse analysis provided by DharmaNexus, the *Bhāvanāvāra* shares substantial internal textual parallels with another section of the *Yamaka*, the *Pajahanavāra* (Ya 7.2.3), comprising 87 matching passages (5,818 shared characters), with the longest segment match running between §3.1–4.1 and §399.1–400.1 [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral does not record any direct external parallels in other canonical corpora, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting its threshold [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral notes one modern translation of the text [SuttaCentral].

None of the secondary literature passages located by keyword search directly address Ya 9.3; they instead discuss the general Buddhist concept of *bhāvanā* (mental cultivation or meditation), discourses such as the *Samādhibhāvanā Sutta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya, or late medieval meditation manuals.
